title: Power to Heal and Forgive
backstory: Jesus has been healing so many people in Capernaum that when evening comes, all the city is gathered together at one door (Mark 1:21-33). The scribes are watching him now, and when he tells a man who cannot walk that his sins are forgiven, they reason in their hearts, "who can forgive sins but God only?" (Mark 2:6-7). That is the question these stories answer: he forgives and he heals, he teaches the mystery of God's kingdom from a boat in a story about seed and soil (Mark 4:1-11), and then he speaks to a storm until even the wind and the sea obey him (Mark 4:41).

passages.synopsis: So many people pack the house in Capernaum that no one else can get near the door. Four friends carry a man who cannot walk up to the roof, break it open, and lower his bed down to Jesus. Seeing their faith, Jesus first tells the man his sins are forgiven — which shocks the scribes, since only God can forgive sins. To show he has that very power, Jesus tells the man to rise, take up his bed, and walk, and he does, before them all.

By the seaside, Jesus sees Levi the tax collector sitting at his booth and says, "Follow me." Levi gets up and follows, and soon Jesus is eating at his house with many publicans and sinners. The scribes and Pharisees grumble about the company he keeps. Jesus answers that healthy people do not need a physician — he came to call sinners, not the righteous.

The crowd by the sea grows so large that Jesus teaches from a boat. He tells of a sower whose seed falls in different places — on the hard path, on stony ground, among thorns, and on good soil. Only the seed in good ground grows up and bears fruit, some thirty, some sixty, some a hundredfold. "He that hath ears to hear," Jesus says, "let him hear."

That evening Jesus and his disciples set out across the sea, and a great storm rises until the ship is filling with water. Jesus is asleep on a pillow in the stern, and the frightened disciples wake him. He rises and says to the sea, "Peace, be still," and there is a great calm. The disciples ask one another what manner of man this is, that even the wind and the sea obey him.

hangmanWords.hint: Town where four friends opened a roof
Jesus said the sick need one, not the whole
Jesus slept on this during the storm
It filled the ship with waves until Jesus spoke

triviaQuestions.question: How did the four friends bring the sick man to Jesus?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Mark 2:4 — "And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay."

triviaQuestions.question: What did Jesus say first to the man sick of the palsy?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Mark 2:5 — "When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee."

triviaQuestions.question: What did Jesus say to the wind and the sea?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Mark 4:39 — "And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm."

triviaQuestions.question: Who was sitting at the receipt of custom when Jesus said, "Follow me"?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Mark 2:14 — "And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him."

reflection: The four friends could not heal their friend, but they could carry him to Jesus. Who could you bring to Jesus in prayer today?
